To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the family of criteria that we characterize consists of the following criteria: (1) The expected utility criterion, which compares sets of consequences on the basis of the expectation of a given utility function.

(1) the set of all probability functions taking strictly positive values on the universe of alternatives and the set of all utility functions defined on the universe of alternative are the only parameters that are necessary for the construction of a complete and consistent ranking of decisions under ignorance or objective uncertainty; and (2) the ranking of decisions is based solely on the expected value of utility, where utility can be defined in any way, as long as the probability function is strictly positive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (a) What is an adequate representation of a completely uncertain decision?
the problem of ranking alternatives when one is uncertain about the probabilities of their consequences.
the problem of ranking decisions under uncertainty and/or ambiguity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a decision maker's preferences satisfy the conditions of our theorem if and only if the decision maker is indifferent between two alternatives if and only if they have the same expected utility, where the probability measure is chosen so as to maximize the expected utility of one alternative relative to that of the other, and the expected utility is computed according to some utility function.

the family of criteria is characterized by two properties: (i) the criterion is a conditional expected utility criterion for some probability function and some utility function; (ii) the probability function is strictly positive and the utility function is defined on the whole set of alternatives.
the set of all criteria that satisfy the axioms is a family of conditional expected utility criteria, for some probability and utility functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a unified framework for decision making under uncertainty and/or ambiguity, and that we show that the criteria that are commonly used for these problems, such as the maximin, maximax, Hurwicz, minimax regret, and Savage, can be obtained from this family of criteria.
we provide an axiometric justification for a wide variety of decision-making criteria under uncertainty or ambiguity.
we have provided an axiomatic foundation for the theory of expected utility under complete ignorance and objective ambiguity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, under certain conditions, a criterion that is based on conditional expected utility is the best possible way to rank uncertain and/or ambiguous choices.
the set of all such criteria is the largest family of criteria that satisfy a set of axioms that are natural extensions of standard expected utility axioms.
the set of all probability distributions over the prices of an ambiguous decision is a complete representation of the decision.
